To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the overexpression of PAI-1 in endothelial cells inhibits the migration of SMCs, but not the adhesion of SMCs.
the endothelial cell over-expression of PAI-1 inhibits the migration of SMC in a cell-cell contact dependent manner.
the overexpression of PAI-1 by ECs in vitro and in vivo leads to a reduction in SMC migration, which is definitely associated with a reduction in SDF-1/CXCR4 manifestation and signaling in SMCs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of PAI-1 in the pathogenesis of vascular disease.

the effect of endothelial overexpression of plasmogen activator inhibitor type 1 (PAI-1) on vascular smooth muscle cell migration, which is an important process in the development of atherosclerotic lesions.
the effects of PAI-1 overexpression on the migratory capacity of endothelial cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of our studies support the hypothesis that PAI-1 plays a significant role in modulating vascular remodeling and neointima formation.
the effects of PII-1 on cell migration are complex and depend on the cell type, its phenotype and the experimental model.
the effect of endothelial overexpression of PAI-1 on smooth-muscle cell migration is not as simple as previously thought.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the endothelial cell is really a dynamic participant in atherosclerosis, and its own role in vascular disease is not confined to the production of a static barrier to the migration of inflammatory cells and smooth muscle cell migration into the intima.

the endothelium can be a dynamic participant in the pathogenesis of vascular illnesses, including atherosclerosis and restenosis. 1,2 The endothelium can regulate vascular tone,3 and it is also mixed up in regulation of vascular development and differentiation.4-6 The endothelium regulates vascular development through the discharge of development elements, such as for example vascular endothelial development aspect (VEGF), and through the discharge of matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs).7

the overexpression of plasmogen activator inhibitor type 1 (PAI-1) by endothelial cells (ECs) inhibits the migration of vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) by reducing the activation of matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) and by increasing the activation of tissue inhibitors of MMPs (TIMPs).
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified an important role for PAI-1 in the regulation of smooth muscle cell (SMC) migration and the development of atherosclerosis.
we can make a significant difference in the lives of our patients by taking a holistic approach.
the endothelium is a dynamic and active component of the vessel wall.
